question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit outbound recipient allowlist now, and should it be Slack-specific channel config or a shared human-chat outbound target policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds a security-sensitive public config/API surface and overlaps broader outbound guardrail work, so automation should not choose the permanent policy boundary.

options.title: Add shared outbound target policy
options.body: Define a channel-agnostic recipient allowlist contract and apply it through the shared outbound send path before Slack-specific delivery.

options.title: Limit to Slack allowTo first
options.body: Ship a narrower Slack config and enforcement path now, accepting possible later migration into a shared policy model.

options.title: Fold into broader guardrails
options.body: Keep this issue tracked under #87870 and defer a standalone allowlist until the sanitizer and verified-delivery design is settled.

recommendation.title: Add shared outbound target policy
recommendation.body: Define a channel-agnostic recipient allowlist contract and apply it through the shared outbound send path before Slack-specific delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is tied to the current message CLI/outbound policy lineage and is the best available owner for choosing the public policy boundary.
